blocks.content: While the Comptroller and Auditor General acts as the guardian of the public purse through financial audit, the Finance Commission serves as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.

rows: Audits revenue and expenditure of Union and States
Recommends distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States
Term of 6 years or until age of 65 years
Constituted every 5 years by the President

items: CAG reports are examined in detail by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament.
Finance Commission recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding on the central government.
CAG can only be removed from office in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CAG is established under Article 148 as the guardian of the public purse, auditing all accounts and expenditure of Union and State governments.
Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body constituted under Article 280 every five years by the President of India.
CAG submits three audit reports to the President regarding appropriation accounts, finance accounts, and public undertakings.
Finance Commission makes crucial recommendations regarding tax devolution between the Centre and States and grants-in-aid under Article 275.
